standaloneRustConsumer: passed with the romedb-production profile; 335 registry/git package identities match the workspace lockfile
upgradeRestore: Passed from the 0.2.13 to 0.2.21 packages on Node 22.0.0 and 24.19.0 (groups v0213-upgrade-restore to v0221-upgrade-restore). 0.2.13 is the floor: it changed the stored value prefix, and earlier files are refused. A collection with a full-text index that folds accents or stems words uses catalog version 10, which 0.2.21 and earlier refuse.

engine.exceptions: the maintained engine exceptions retained, one added: FTS folding and stemming (romedb/docs/core-exceptions.md)
engine.storageFormat: __romedb_ schema prefix, .romedb extension, stored values prefixed RDB 01 (FDB 01 before 0.2.13); openEmbedded and serve use MVCC files; collections with a * array path index use catalog version 8, others keep version 7 or earlier; collections with a weighted full-text index use catalog version 9; collections with a folded or stemmed full-text index use catalog version 10
engine.change: one engine core patch: the fold and stemmer WITH keys in core/index_method/fts add Tantivy AsciiFoldingFilter and the Snowball Stemmer as an analyzer registered under its own name, and prefix expansion builds the expanded words as term queries, so a stored stem is never stemmed again. rusqlite 0.41.1 (bundled SQLite 3.54.1) and Rust 1.89 for RUSTSEC-2026-0459. Same upstream as 0.2.21 (Turso v0.8.3, Tantivy 0.27.0)

spatial.explainReadsNoData: metered EXPLAIN reports zero rows read for every spatial form (spatial_explain_reads_no_documents_or_index_entries)

supportedScope.ownership: One owning process per database file; shared clients connect to its service

resolvedForRelease: RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (CVE-2026-119375, SQLite before 3.54.0 can return uninitialized memory when it opens a database whose -wal file has a different page size): rusqlite 0.41.1 bundles SQLite 3.54.1 through libsqlite3-sys 0.39.1; the workspace builds with Rust 1.89, which rusqlite 0.41 needs

documentationOverrides.ENVELOPE.md: Historical 2.1.0 measurements; the raw-evidence link points to the immutable fastdb-v2.1.0 release

performance: Historical 2.1.0 operating envelope retained; fresh bounded application sample, not capacity guarantees
buildHost: Built and qualified under scripts/romedb-heavy (shared lock, two jobs, cgroup memory ceiling)
publication: Qualified for publication; anonymous public-download verification is separate
